after: Browsers give headings, paragraphs, and other parts some starting styles. Your CSS can change those styles. You do not need to clear every starting style first. CodeQuest already connects your CSS editor to the project’s HTML.

On your own computer, an HTML page can load a separate CSS file.

Put this line inside `head`. `rel="stylesheet"` says the file contains styles. `href="styles.css"` gives its location. Save that CSS file beside the HTML file. CodeQuest’s project uses its own CSS editor instead.

CSS skips a setting whose value it cannot use. If you write `twelve-pixels` instead of `12px`, that padding setting will not work. The valid teal color can still work. A missing brace or broken selector can affect more code, so check those too.

before.question: If only padding-left becomes twelve-pixels, does that invalid value remove the valid teal color too?
choices: Yes; every invalid value deletes the entire stylesheet.
No; that padding declaration is discarded, while the valid color can still apply.
It automatically converts the English word to 12px.
before.explanation: Separate valid declarations can still participate in the cascade. This does not mean every kind of CSS syntax error has the same recovery boundary.

after.question: You change only the padding value to twelve-pixels. What happens to the valid teal color?
choices: It disappears because every CSS rule is deleted.
It can still apply; only the invalid padding setting is skipped.
The browser turns the words into 12px.
after.explanation: Each setting has its own value. The invalid padding value does not remove the valid color setting.
